newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Pullback in US T-bonds seen short-lived.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Pullback in US T-bonds seen short-lived.

text.p: U.S. Treasury bond futures' downturn on Tuesday is likely to be short-lived, given the strong trending upmoves the market has made in recent weeks, technical analysts said.

"The fact that we're getting a pullback today doesn't come as too much of a surprise," said Eric Wall, a senior technical analyst at MMS International. "Last week's rally and its continuation yesterday kept oscillators in overbought territory and that's causing some mild liquidation."
September T-bond futures were off 10/32 at 111-24/32 in mid-morning trade.
Earlier in the day, the contract extended its recent gains to a four-month high of 112-10/32 before stalling.
Analysts said the market had been due for some correction.
"My biggest concern at this point is the fact that we're heavily over-extended," Wall said.

"A mild case of bearish divergence" was forming on the daily stochastic, he noted, and an "outside day" -- a minor reversal pattern -- was developing on the daily chart, pointing to some consolidative trading in the near term.
But a recoil here would relieve the overbought conditions and set up a base for further gains, Wall said.
He expected the market's pullback to be limited to the June 6 high of 111-9/32, or in the worst-case scenario the May 13 high of 110-9/32.
"You have to realize that the advance since April has been impulsive in nature and that suggests we have continuation higher to go," Wall said.

John Gambino of JBG Technical Analysis, an Elliott Wave watcher, expected some slightly bigger correction, noting that the market might have seen the end of a medium-term five-wave sequence that had started from the mid-April lows.
He said a 50- to 62-percent correction of that two-month advance, down toward the 109 or 108-1/2 area, was possible in coming weeks, although the market was still bullish in the long term.
He said he would not add longs now but would be more willing to buy bonds should prices retreat toward 109.
"I suspect this is just one of a series of five-wave sequences," Gambino said of the gains in the past two months.
-- Shin Kishima/Chicago Derivatives Desk ((312-408-8750)) E-mail: derivatives@reuters.com
